column2:
habitat(n.)棲息地、自然環境
inhabit(v.)居住於
natural habitat 自然棲地
habitat loss 棲地喪失
Habitat loss is the biggest threat to many wild animals.
(棲地喪失是許多野生動物面臨的最大威脅。)
It is better to see animals in their natural habitat than in a zoo.
(在自然棲地看動物比在動物園看更好。)

haul(v./n.)拖、拉、搬運、一次的收穫量
(無詞性變化)
haul up 拖上來
in the long haul 長期來看
The fishermen hauled their nets onto the boat.
(漁夫們把漁網拖上船。)
Learning a language takes effort, but it pays off in the long haul.
(學語言需要努力，但長遠來看是值得的。)

hazard(n./v.)危險、危害、冒險提出
hazardous(adj.)有危險的
health hazard 健康危害
fire hazard 火災隱患
Smoking is a serious health hazard for both smokers and people around them.
(吸菸對吸菸者及周遭的人都是嚴重的健康危害。)
Piles of old newspapers in the hallway are a fire hazard.
(走廊上堆積的舊報紙是一種火災隱患。)

heir(n.)繼承人、後繼者
heiress(n.)女繼承人
heir to the throne 王位繼承人
sole heir 唯一繼承人
Prince William is heir to the British throne.
(威廉王子是英國王位的繼承人。)
As the sole heir, she inherited her grandfather's entire fortune.
(身為唯一繼承人，她繼承了祖父全部的財產。)

hence(adv.)因此、從此以後
(無詞性變化)
hence the name 因此得名
two years hence 兩年後
The island is shaped like a turtle, hence the name Turtle Island.
(這座島的形狀像烏龜，因此得名龜山島。)
The road was blocked by a landslide; hence, we had to turn back.
(道路被土石流阻斷，因此我們必須折返。)

herb(n.)香草、草藥
herbal(adj.)草藥的
herbal tea 花草茶
Chinese herbs 中藥材
My grandmother grows herbs like basil and mint on her balcony.
(我奶奶在陽台上種了羅勒和薄荷等香草。)
Some people drink herbal tea to help them relax before bed.
(有些人睡前喝花草茶來幫助放鬆。)

heritage(n.)遺產、傳統、文化遺產
(無詞性變化)
cultural heritage 文化遺產
World Heritage Site 世界遺產
The old temple is an important part of the town's cultural heritage.
(這座古廟是小鎮文化遺產中重要的一部分。)
The Great Wall of China is a famous World Heritage Site.
(中國的萬里長城是著名的世界遺產。)

highlight(v./n.)強調、突顯、最精彩的部分
highlighter(n.)螢光筆
the highlight of 的最精彩部分
highlight the importance of 強調…的重要性
The fireworks show was the highlight of our trip to Taipei.
(煙火秀是我們台北之旅最精彩的部分。)
The report highlights the importance of getting enough sleep.
(這份報告強調充足睡眠的重要性。)

hockey(n.)曲棍球
(無詞性變化)
ice hockey 冰上曲棍球
field hockey 草地曲棍球
Ice hockey is one of the most popular sports in Canada.
(冰上曲棍球是加拿大最受歡迎的運動之一。)
Our school's field hockey team won the national championship.
(我們學校的曲棍球隊贏得了全國冠軍。)

honorable(adj.)可敬的、光榮的、正直的
honor(n./v.)榮譽、尊敬
honorably(adv.)光榮地、正直地
an honorable man 正直的人
honorable mention 佳作、榮譽獎
Returning the lost wallet was an honorable thing to do.
(歸還遺失的錢包是一件值得敬佩的事。)
My drawing received an honorable mention in the art contest.
(我的畫作在美術比賽中獲得了佳作。)

horizontal(adj./n.)水平的、橫的、水平線
horizon(n.)地平線
vertical(adj.)垂直的
horizontal line 水平線
horizontal axis 橫軸
Draw a horizontal line across the middle of the page.
(在頁面中間畫一條水平線。)
The horizontal axis of the graph shows the years.
(這張圖表的橫軸表示年份。)

hormone(n.)荷爾蒙、激素
hormonal(adj.)荷爾蒙的
growth hormone 生長激素
stress hormone 壓力荷爾蒙
Teenagers go through many hormone changes during puberty.
(青少年在青春期會經歷許多荷爾蒙變化。)
Getting enough sleep helps the body produce growth hormone.
(充足的睡眠有助於身體分泌生長激素。)

hostage(n.)人質
(無詞性變化)
take sb. hostage 挾持某人為人質
release hostages 釋放人質
The robbers took three bank workers hostage.
(搶匪挾持了三名銀行員工作為人質。)
After hours of talks, all the hostages were released safely.
(經過數小時的談判，所有人質都被安全釋放。)

hostile(adj.)敵對的、懷有敵意的、不友善的
hostility(n.)敵意
be hostile to 對…懷有敵意
hostile environment 惡劣的環境
The villagers were hostile to the idea of building a factory nearby.
(村民們強烈反對在附近蓋工廠的想法。)
Few plants can survive in such a hostile environment.
(很少植物能在如此惡劣的環境中生存。)

hostility(n.)敵意、敵對、戰爭行為
hostile(adj.)敵對的
hostility toward 對…的敵意
open hostility 公開的敵意
He felt hostility from his new classmates on the first day.
(第一天他就感受到新同學對他的敵意。)
The two countries finally agreed to end their hostilities.
(兩國終於同意停止敵對行動。)

housing(n.)住房、住宅、房屋供給
house(n./v.)房屋、收容
housing prices 房價
public housing 公共住宅、社會住宅
High housing prices make it hard for young people to buy a home.
(高房價讓年輕人很難買房。)
The city plans to build more public housing for low-income families.
(市政府計畫為低收入家庭興建更多社會住宅。)

howl(n./v.)嚎叫、怒吼、哀號
(無詞性變化)
howl with laughter 捧腹大笑
the howl of the wind 風的呼嘯聲
We could hear wolves howling in the distance.
(我們能聽到遠處狼群的嚎叫聲。)
The audience howled with laughter at the comedian's jokes.
(觀眾被那位喜劇演員的笑話逗得捧腹大笑。)

hypothesis(n.)假說、假設
hypotheses(n.)假說(複數)
hypothetical(adj.)假設的
test a hypothesis 驗證假說
support a hypothesis 支持假說
Scientists design experiments to test their hypotheses.
(科學家設計實驗來驗證他們的假說。)
The new data supports the hypothesis that the climate is getting warmer.
(新的數據支持了氣候正在變暖的假說。)

icon(n.)圖示、偶像、象徵
iconic(adj.)代表性的、標誌性的
fashion icon 時尚偶像
click on the icon 點選圖示
Click on the icon at the top of the screen to open the app.
(點選螢幕上方的圖示來開啟應用程式。)
Taipei 101 has become an icon of Taiwan.
(台北101已經成為台灣的象徵。)

ideology(n.)意識形態、思想體系
ideological(adj.)意識形態的
political ideology 政治意識形態
ideological differences 意識形態的差異
The two parties have very different political ideologies.
(這兩個政黨的政治意識形態大不相同。)
Ideological differences sometimes make it hard for people to cooperate.
(意識形態的差異有時讓人們很難合作。)

idiot(n.)白痴、傻瓜
idiotic(adj.)愚蠢的
feel like an idiot 覺得自己像個傻瓜
a complete idiot 十足的笨蛋
I felt like an idiot when I realized I had gone to the wrong classroom.
(當我發現自己走錯教室時，覺得自己像個傻瓜。)
Only an idiot would drive that fast in heavy rain.
(只有笨蛋才會在大雨中開那麼快。)

illusion(n.)錯覺、幻想、假象
illusory(adj.)虛幻的
optical illusion 視覺錯覺
be under the illusion that 誤以為…
This picture is an optical illusion; the two lines are actually the same length.
(這張圖是一種視覺錯覺，兩條線其實一樣長。)
He was under the illusion that he could pass the test without studying.
(他誤以為自己不用讀書就能通過考試。)

immense(adj.)巨大的、極大的
immensely(adv.)極其、非常
immense pressure 巨大的壓力
an immense amount of 大量的…
Senior high school students often face immense pressure before the college entrance exam.
(高中生在大學入學考試前常面臨巨大的壓力。)
Building the bridge took an immense amount of time and money.
(建造這座橋花費了大量的時間和金錢。)

immune(adj.)免疫的、不受影響的、豁免的
immunity(n.)免疫力
immune system 免疫系統
be immune to 對…免疫、不受…影響
Regular exercise can help strengthen your immune system.
(規律運動有助於強化你的免疫系統。)
No one is completely immune to criticism.
(沒有人能完全不受批評的影響。)

implement(v./n.)實施、執行、工具
implementation(n.)實施、執行
implement a policy 實施政策
farm implements 農具
The school will implement a new uniform policy next semester.
(學校下學期將實施新的制服規定。)
The museum displays old farm implements used by early settlers.
(博物館展示早期移民使用過的舊農具。)

implication(n.)可能的影響、含意、牽連
imply(v.)暗示、意味
have implications for 對…有影響
by implication 言下之意
The new law will have serious implications for small businesses.
(新法將對小型企業造成嚴重的影響。)
He said the plan was risky and, by implication, that we should not try it.
(他說這個計畫有風險，言下之意是我們不該嘗試。)

impulse(n.)衝動、推動力、脈衝
impulsive(adj.)衝動的
on impulse 一時衝動
impulse buying 衝動購物
I bought these shoes on impulse, but I don't really need them.
(我一時衝動買了這雙鞋，但其實並不需要。)
Online sales often encourage impulse buying.
(網路特賣常常助長衝動購物。)

incentive(n./adj.)誘因、動機、獎勵的
(無詞性變化)
tax incentive 租稅優惠
incentive to do 做…的動機
The government offers tax incentives to companies that use green energy.
(政府對使用綠色能源的公司提供租稅優惠。)
Good grades can be an incentive for students to study harder.
(好成績可以成為學生更努力讀書的動力。)

incorporate(v.)包含、納入、合併
incorporation(n.)納入、合併
incorporate A into B 把A納入B
incorporated company 股份有限公司
The teacher incorporated games into her English lessons.
(老師把遊戲融入她的英文課中。)
The new design incorporates many suggestions from students.
(新的設計納入了許多學生的建議。)

index(n./v.)索引、指數、指標、編入索引
indices(n.)指數(複數)
price index 物價指數
index finger 食指
You can find the word quickly by looking it up in the index.
(你可以從索引中查找，很快就能找到這個字。)
The air quality index was very high in the city yesterday.
(昨天市區的空氣品質指標非常高。)

indifferent(adj.)漠不關心的、冷淡的、平庸的
indifference(n.)冷漠
be indifferent to 對…漠不關心
an indifferent attitude 冷淡的態度
How can people be indifferent to the suffering of others?
(人們怎麼能對他人的苦難漠不關心呢？)
His indifferent attitude toward his studies worried his parents.
(他對課業漠不關心的態度讓他父母很擔心。)

indigenous(adj.)原住民的、本土的、原生的
(無詞性變化)
indigenous peoples 原住民族
indigenous species 原生物種
Taiwan has sixteen officially recognized indigenous peoples.
(台灣有十六個官方認定的原住民族。)
The Formosan black bear is an indigenous species of Taiwan.
(台灣黑熊是台灣的原生物種。)

indispensable(adj.)不可或缺的、必需的
dispensable(adj.)非必要的
indispensable to/for 對…不可或缺
an indispensable tool 不可或缺的工具
Smartphones have become an indispensable tool in modern life.
(智慧型手機已經成為現代生活中不可或缺的工具。)
Clean water is indispensable to human survival.
(乾淨的水對人類生存是不可或缺的。)

indulge(v.)沉溺、縱容、盡情享受
indulgence(n.)沉溺、放縱
indulgent(adj.)縱容的
indulge in 沉迷於、盡情享受
indulge a child 寵溺孩子
After the exam, I indulged in a big bowl of shaved ice.
(考完試後，我盡情享受了一大碗剉冰。)
Grandparents often indulge their grandchildren with sweets and toys.
(祖父母常用糖果和玩具寵溺孫子女。)

inevitable(adj.)不可避免的、必然的
inevitably(adv.)不可避免地
an inevitable result 必然的結果
it is inevitable that 無可避免的是…
Making mistakes is an inevitable part of learning.
(犯錯是學習過程中無可避免的一部分。)
It was inevitable that prices would rise after the typhoon.
(颱風過後物價上漲是必然的。)

infect(v.)傳染、感染、影響
infection(n.)感染
infectious(adj.)傳染性的
be infected with 感染…
infected wound 受感染的傷口
Thousands of people were infected with the virus last winter.
(去年冬天有數千人感染了這種病毒。)
Her laughter infected everyone in the room.
(她的笑聲感染了房間裡的每一個人。)

infinite(adj.)無限的、無窮的
infinity(n.)無限
infinitely(adv.)無限地、極其
infinite patience 無比的耐心
infinite possibilities 無限的可能
The kindergarten teacher showed infinite patience with the children.
(那位幼兒園老師對孩子們展現了無比的耐心。)
Young people have infinite possibilities for the future.
(年輕人的未來有無限的可能。)

infrastructure(n.)基礎建設、公共設施
(無詞性變化)
public infrastructure 公共基礎建設
transportation infrastructure 交通建設
The government plans to spend billions on public infrastructure.
(政府計畫投入數十億元於公共基礎建設。)
Good transportation infrastructure helps the economy grow.
(良好的交通建設有助於經濟成長。)

inherent(adj.)固有的、內在的、天生的
inherently(adv.)本質上
inherent in 為…所固有
inherent risk 固有的風險
There are risks inherent in every extreme sport.
(每一項極限運動都有其固有的風險。)
Curiosity is an inherent part of human nature.
(好奇心是人性中固有的一部分。)

inherit(v.)繼承、遺傳、接手
inheritance(n.)遺產、繼承
heir(n.)繼承人
inherit from 從…繼承
inherit a fortune 繼承財產
She inherited her mother's talent for music.
(她遺傳了母親的音樂天分。)
He inherited the family restaurant from his father.
(他從父親那裡接手了家族餐廳。)

initiate(v./adj./n.)開始、發起、使入會、新入會者
initiation(n.)開始、入會儀式
initiative(n.)倡議、主動性
initiate a conversation 開啟對話
initiate a project 發起計畫
Shy students often find it hard to initiate a conversation.
(害羞的學生常常很難主動開啟對話。)
The student council initiated a project to reduce plastic waste on campus.
(學生會發起了一項減少校園塑膠垃圾的計畫。)

initiative(n./adj.)主動性、倡議、新方案、起始的
initiate(v.)發起
take the initiative 採取主動
on one's own initiative 主動地
She took the initiative to organize a beach cleanup.
(她主動籌辦了一場淨灘活動。)
The city launched a new initiative to encourage people to ride bikes.
(市政府推出一項鼓勵民眾騎腳踏車的新方案。)

inject(v.)注射、注入、投入
injection(n.)注射
inject sth. into 把…注入…
inject money into 投入資金到…
The nurse injected the medicine into the patient's arm.
(護理師把藥物注射到病人的手臂中。)
The new teacher injected fresh energy into the class.
(新老師為班級注入了一股新的活力。)

injection(n.)注射、打針、(資金)投入
inject(v.)注射
give sb. an injection 幫某人打針
an injection of cash 資金注入
The doctor gave the child an injection to lower his fever.
(醫生幫那孩子打了一針退燒。)
The company needs an injection of cash to survive.
(這家公司需要資金挹注才能生存下去。)

inning(n.)(棒球)局
innings(n.)(板球)局、一局
the ninth inning 第九局
the top of the inning 上半局
Our team scored three runs in the ninth inning and won the game.
(我們隊在第九局得了三分，贏得了比賽。)
The pitcher was replaced in the bottom of the sixth inning.
(那位投手在六局下半被換下場。)

innovation(n.)創新、新發明
innovate(v.)創新
innovative(adj.)創新的
technological innovation 科技創新
encourage innovation 鼓勵創新
Technological innovation has changed the way we learn.
(科技創新改變了我們學習的方式。)
The company encourages innovation by rewarding new ideas.
(這家公司以獎勵新點子的方式鼓勵創新。)

innovative(adj.)創新的、新穎的
innovation(n.)創新
innovate(v.)創新
innovative design 創新設計
innovative approach 創新的方法
The students came up with an innovative design for a solar-powered car.
(學生們想出了一個太陽能車的創新設計。)
Our teacher uses innovative approaches to make history lessons fun.
(我們老師用創新的方法讓歷史課變得有趣。)

inquiry(n.)詢問、調查、探究
inquire(v.)詢問、調查
make inquiries 詢問、打聽
an inquiry into 對…的調查
We received many inquiries about the summer camp.
(我們接到許多關於夏令營的詢問。)
The government ordered an inquiry into the cause of the fire.
(政府下令調查這場火災的起因。)

insane(adj.)瘋狂的、荒唐的、精神失常的
insanity(n.)精神失常、瘋狂
drive sb. insane 把某人逼瘋
an insane idea 瘋狂的主意
The noise from the construction site is driving me insane.
(工地傳來的噪音快把我逼瘋了。)
Riding a bike across Taiwan in three days sounds insane.
(三天騎腳踏車環島聽起來很瘋狂。)

insight(n.)洞察力、深刻見解
insightful(adj.)有洞察力的
gain insight into 深入了解…
valuable insight 寶貴的見解
Volunteering at the hospital gave me insight into a doctor's daily life.
(在醫院當志工讓我深入了解醫生的日常生活。)
The speaker shared valuable insights about studying abroad.
(講者分享了關於出國留學的寶貴見解。)

installation(n.)安裝、設置、裝置藝術
install(v.)安裝
software installation 軟體安裝
art installation 裝置藝術
The installation of the new air conditioners will take two days.
(安裝新冷氣將需要兩天的時間。)
The art installation in the park attracted many visitors.
(公園裡的裝置藝術吸引了許多遊客。)

institute(n./v.)機構、學院、研究所、設立、制定
institution(n.)機構、制度
research institute 研究機構
institute a policy 制定政策
She works at a research institute that studies earthquakes.
(她在一間研究地震的研究機構工作。)
The school instituted a new rule to ban phones in class.
(學校制定了一項上課禁止使用手機的新規定。)

institution(n.)機構、制度、慣例
institute(n./v.)機構、設立
institutional(adj.)機構的、制度上的
financial institution 金融機構
educational institution 教育機構
Banks and insurance companies are financial institutions.
(銀行和保險公司都是金融機構。)
Marriage is one of the oldest social institutions.
(婚姻是最古老的社會制度之一。)

intact(adj.)完整無缺的、未受損的
(無詞性變化)
remain intact 保持完整
fully intact 完好無缺
Amazingly, the old temple remained intact after the earthquake.
(令人驚訝的是，那座古廟在地震後仍完好無缺。)
The package arrived with everything inside intact.
(包裹送達時裡面的東西都完好無損。)

integrate(v.)整合、使融入、結合
integration(n.)整合、融入
integrated(adj.)整合的
integrate into 融入…
integrate A with B 將A與B結合
It took the new students a few weeks to integrate into the class.
(新同學花了幾週才融入班級。)
The course integrates science with art in creative ways.
(這門課以富有創意的方式將科學與藝術結合。)
